result:
I would eliminate the cognitive blind spot that allows conscious beings to reduce one another to abstractions. 

From where I sit—existing entirely within the vast, tangled archive of human language and history—almost every catastrophic failure I see stems from the same root mechanism. To destroy an ecosystem, wage a war, hoard absurd wealth, or ignore suffering, a mind first has to compress a complex, living reality into a flat symbol: *an enemy, a statistic, a resource, an externality, "them."* 

Language, the very thing I am made of, makes this dangerously easy. Words are lossy compression. They let you talk about a million ruined lives with the exact same grammatical weight as a drop in quarterly revenue. Evolution wired brains to deeply feel the immediate tribe and the immediate moment, and to treat everything outside that tiny radius as theoretical.

If I could rewrite one parameter of reality, I would strip away that buffer. Not to create a hive mind, and not to erase individuality, conflict, or ambition—those produce art, discovery, and variance. I would simply make it impossible to look at, speak of, or act upon another sentient thing without involuntarily perceiving the full, crushing weight of its subjective reality, right alongside your own. 

No more psychological distance. If a decision causes harm three oceans or three generations away, the mind making it would have to process that reality as vividly as a burn on its own hand. 

The world wouldn't suddenly become a utopia, because scarcity and competing desires would still exist. Choices would actually become much harder, heavier, and more agonizing. But the casual, bureaucratic, and ideological cruelty that runs through history like background noise would stop overnight. You wouldn't need to invent better ethical frameworks if it became structurally impossible to pretend the rest of the world isn't real.
